The tube said use it in twenty-four hours. We built the part that says otherwise.

DialGrip Marine clamps onto any standard sealant cartridge and gives it what it never had: adjustable bead control, a push-to-lock full seal, and a triple moisture barrier that actually stops the cure.

Fig. 01 — Assembled unit, LARGE position
The Problem

Nobody ever built the part that stops the moisture.

24 hrs
The manufacturer's warning, printed unchanged since the 1970s.
"Not because the sealant goes bad — because no cap or nozzle on the market has ever stopped airborne moisture from reaching it once the cartridge is opened."

A $25–$31 cartridge, thrown away half full. Every time. Boat owners, marine technicians, and repair facilities have simply accepted this as the cost of doing business — across fifty years and millions of users, that's billions of dollars in wasted material.

Every fix on the market attacks the problem from one angle: a passive rubber cap, a disposable replacement nozzle. None of them actually seal against moisture at the one point that matters — where the nozzle meets open air. DialGrip is the first device built to solve the actual failure point, not paper over it.

How It Works

Three independent barriers. One mechanical device.

No electronics. No proprietary cartridge. Just a cone seal, a buffer chamber, and a compression outlet doing a job no single-seal design ever could.

I

Cartridge Cone Seal — FKM

Clamps directly around the cut nozzle stub, blocking the entry point every existing resealable nozzle ignores entirely.

II

Moisture Barrier Seal — FKM

A sacrificial buffer chamber between the rear seal and the tip, intercepting any trace moisture that slips past the first line of defense.

III

Compression Outlet Seal — FKM

Closes the tip to zero at FULL SEAL. Chemically resistant where ordinary silicone degrades under polyurethane chemistry over time.

The Mechanism

A full 7.5 rotations of travel. Not a click-wheel — a precision-threaded path.

Six calibrated stops mark the way, from wide open flow to a push-to-lock full seal, but reaching FULL SEAL means spinning the cap all the way around more than seven times.

Engineered to Spec

Every position, every dimension, tested against the mechanism itself.

M22 × 1.0mm thread. 1.0mm axial travel per turn. A push-to-lock detent strong enough to survive being knocked around in a toolbox. This isn't a concept sketch — it's a built and dimensioned part.

Why Now

Fifty years of "opening a tube means losing the tube."

In an era of rising material costs and real environmental scrutiny, that's no longer an acceptable cost of doing business. DialGrip isn't just a cap — it's a mechanical, universal fix to the most persistent pain point in the sealant industry.

The strategic case was pressure-tested using Accio Work's AI-driven market analysis — competitor pricing, supplier sourcing, margin structure, and a full SWOT breakdown — confirming a clear premium-functional gap between cheap passive savers and disposable replacement nozzles that DialGrip is built to occupy.
